title: White light and colour
keyIdea: White light is a mixture of colours. A prism refracts each colour by a different amount, so it spreads them into a spectrum: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet. Red has the lowest frequency and bends least; violet has the highest frequency and bends most. A second prism can turn the colours back into white, so the glass adds nothing. An object looks coloured because it reflects some colours and absorbs the rest: a red shirt reflects red. In light with no red in it, it reflects nothing and looks black. A filter lets its own colour through and absorbs the others, so filters only take light away.
familyTip: On a sunny day, hold a glass of water or an old CD in the sun and look for the spectrum. Ask your child which colour is at each end and which bends most. In a dark room, put red cellophane over a phone torch and look at a blue toy: what colour does it look, and why?

visual.caption: Is it true of white light and colour? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: Violet bends more than red in a prism
The prism adds colour to the light
A red shirt in blue light looks black
A red filter adds red to white light
A white object reflects all colours
Coloured lights mix just like paint

lab.caption: Flagship lab: name the bands of a prism's spectrum, rejoin them with a second prism, light shirts in colour and build filter stacks.

kid: White light is not one colour. It is a mix of many. Shine it into a glass prism and it spreads out into a spectrum: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.

This happens because glass bends, or refracts, each colour by a different amount. Red has the lowest frequency and bends least. Violet has the highest frequency and bends most. Put a second prism the other way up and the colours join back into white.

You see an object's colour from the light it reflects. A red shirt reflects red light and absorbs the rest. A white shirt reflects every colour. A black shirt absorbs them all. In blue light, a red shirt has no red to reflect, so it looks black.
A filter lets its own colour through and absorbs the rest. A red filter turns white light red by taking the other colours away. Put a green filter after it and no light gets through at all.
adult: Ages 11 to 12. The National Curriculum in England (KS3 Physics, Waves) lists colours and the different frequencies of light, white light and prisms (qualitative only), and differential colour effects in absorption and diffuse reflection. Newton showed in 1672 that a prism separates white light and a second prism puts it back together. Key words: spectrum, dispersion, refraction, frequency, wavelength, reflect, absorb, transmit, filter.

The visible spectrum runs from red, about 700 nanometres in wavelength and the lowest frequency, to violet, about 400 nanometres and the highest. Glass slows violet light a little more than red, so violet refracts more; that spreading is called dispersion. Schools model light as red, green and blue parts: yellow is red plus green, cyan is green plus blue, and magenta is red plus blue. In that model, a surface or filter keeps only the parts it shares with the light.

Common mistakes: thinking the prism makes the colours; thinking red bends most because it is first in the list; mixing coloured light like paint, so that a red shirt in blue light is predicted purple; thinking an object keeps its colour in any light; and thinking filters add colour, so that red plus green filters make yellow. Filters only subtract, so red then green lets no light through.

In the lab your child names the seven bands on a screen in frequency order, picks the colour that bent most and puts in a second, upside-down prism to make white again. They predict the colour of shirts under coloured light, build filter stacks to reach a target colour (including a cyan filter), and choose the filter that makes a blue shirt look black or a yellow banana look red.

practice.prompt: White light and colour: which colour of the spectrum bends most in a prism?
practice.hint: Higher frequency bends more. Which end has the highest frequency?
practice.explain: Violet has the highest frequency in the visible spectrum, so glass refracts it most.

practice.prompt: A prism spreads white light into the 7 colours of the spectrum. A card blocks {n} of the colours. How many colours still reach the screen?
practice.hint: Start with all 7 colours, then take away the ones the card blocks.
practice.explain: 7 colours take away {n} blocked colours leaves {=7-n} colours on the screen.

practice.prompt: What colour does a green leaf look in red light?
practice.hint: Which colour does the leaf reflect? Is that colour in the red light?
practice.explain: The leaf reflects green and absorbs other colours. Red light has no green, so nothing is reflected and it looks black.

practice.prompt: On a stage, {n} actors wear blue shirts. The only light is red. How many shirts look black?
practice.hint: Can a blue shirt reflect red light? Think about every shirt.
practice.explain: A blue shirt reflects only blue. There is no blue in red light, so all {n} shirts look black.

practice.prompt: White light goes through a blue filter. What comes out?
practice.hint: A filter transmits its own colour. What does it do to the others?
practice.explain: The blue filter transmits blue and absorbs the other colours, so only blue light comes out.

pool.prompt: Why does a prism spread white light into a spectrum?
choices: Each colour refracts by a different amount
pool.hint: A second prism can turn the colours back into white. What does that tell you?
pool.explain: The colours were already in white light. Glass refracts each frequency by a different amount, so they spread out: dispersion.

pool.prompt: Which list is in order of increasing frequency?
choices: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet
Violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red
Red, yellow, orange, green, indigo, blue, violet
pool.hint: Red has the lowest frequency of visible light and violet the highest.
pool.explain: Frequency rises from red to violet: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.

pool.prompt: What colour does a white T-shirt look under blue light?
pool.hint: A white surface reflects every colour that falls on it. Which colours fall on it here?
pool.explain: A white T-shirt reflects all colours, but only blue light reaches it, so it reflects blue and looks blue.

pool.prompt: White light passes through a red filter and then a green filter. What reaches the screen?
pool.hint: Filters only take colours away. What does the green filter do to red light?
pool.explain: The red filter lets only red through, and the green filter absorbs red, so no light gets through.

pool.prompt: Red light has a wavelength of about 700 nm. Another colour has a wavelength of {n}0 nm. How many nanometres shorter than red is it?
pool.hint: Subtract the shorter wavelength from 700 nm.
pool.explain: 700 nm minus {n}0 nm is {=700-n*10} nm. A shorter wavelength means a higher frequency, nearer the violet end.

pool.prompt: Why does a black object look black in white light?
pool.hint: What reaches your eye from a black surface?
pool.explain: A black object absorbs every colour, so almost no light is reflected to your eye.

pool.prompt: A yellow banana reflects red and green light. Which filter over a white lamp makes it look red?
pool.hint: Which filter lets through a colour the banana reflects, and is that colour red?
pool.explain: A red filter lets only red through. The banana reflects red, so it looks red. A blue filter would make it look black.

pool.prompt: A stage has {n} spotlights. Each has a filter. {k} of them have red filters and the rest have blue filters. How many spotlights make a red costume look black?
pool.hint: A red costume looks black in any light with no red in it. Which spotlights have no red?
pool.explain: The {=n-k} blue spotlights send no red light, so the red costume looks black in them.

pool.prompt: A cyan filter lets green and blue through. Which second filter gives blue light?
pool.hint: The second filter must keep blue and absorb green.
pool.explain: A blue filter keeps the blue from the cyan light and absorbs the green, so blue light comes out.
